preamble: At the end of a word, Sanskrit does not allow the retroflex sibilant [ʂ]. It is replaced by the retroflex stop [ʈ], which is the final-position counterpart of the sibilant in the paradigm.

examples.note: 'hating, enemy', nominative singular. Cf. instrumental plural dviḍbhiḥ.

sources: Whitney, W. D. (1889). Sanskrit Grammar. Harvard University Press.
Burrow, T. (1955). The Sanskrit Language. Faber & Faber.
Macdonell, A. A. (1927). A Sanskrit Grammar for Students. Oxford University Press.
